subject: SLA baseline and exception matrix for Peregrine - proposed terms
messages:
From: Emily Thomas <emily.thomas@peregrinefin.com>

Cc: procurement@peregrinefin.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Baseline SLA and maintenance carveouts

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the infra looked promising. Before we move to legal, procurement asked me to capture a baseline SLA ask so they can compare it against our internal risk model. High level:

- Our critical payment flows run in the 02:00-05:00 UTC window and must remain highly reliable.
- We can tolerate scheduled maintenance, but need a documented exception process and advance notice for any maintenance that may affect the 02:00-06:00 UTC window.
- We want both uptime and latency commitments for hosted endpoints. Specifically, we’d like to see a standard uptime percentage and an approach for monthly service credits.

Can you share a proposed baseline (uptime %, latency p50/p95, monthly credit bands, and any carveouts for scheduled maintenance or batch windows)? If you have an adjusted template that accounts for weekend batch loads, that would be helpful.

Appreciate it — Emily
Emily Thomas

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Baseline SLA and maintenance carveouts

Hi Emily — thanks for outlining the ask. Attached is a first-pass proposal tailored for Peregrine that tries to balance strict availability with pragmatic operational carveouts for scheduled batch windows. High level summary in-line below; full terms in the attached PDF (Redwood-SLA-proposal-peregrine-v1.pdf).

Proposed baseline (hosted API):
- Uptime (monthly): 99.95% standard baseline for production routes.
- Latency commitments: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 350ms (regional, measured at the API gateway).
- Monthly remedy: tiered credit bands: 99.95-99.90 => 5% monthly credit; 99.90-99.50 => 15%; <99.50 => 35% (credits applied to monthly invoice, capped at 100% of that month’s fees).

Exception and maintenance carveouts:
- Scheduled maintenance windows: customers must be notified 72 hours in advance for any maintenance that could impact availability; we propose a maximum of 8 maintenance hours per calendar month that are carve-outs (not counted against uptime).
- Batch window accommodation: for the 02:00-06:00 UTC window you highlighted, we can agree on an "operational buffer" — if you shift non-critical batch ingestion to a secondary pipeline during planned jobs, we will exclude those pipelines from uptime calculation. We’ll document the operational buffer in an appendix.

Additional mitigations we propose:
- Canary ramp and automatic fallback to a compatible smaller model variant for short-term capacity issues (no credits triggered during automatic fallbacks under 30 minutes).
- Detailed incident reports and a monthly availability dashboard (we export raw uptime metrics — will attach uptime-metrics.csv on next internal note).

Ben / Priyom — looping you in for technical/finance guardrails. Emily — if this looks directionally correct I’ll ask legal to prepare an editable DocuSign-ready exhibit.

Best,

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Emily Thomas <emily.thomas@peregrinefin.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Baseline SLA and maintenance carveouts (internal comments and adjusted bands)

A quick internal note and a suggested adjustment before legal drafts final language. I’m pasting the proposed edits and rationale so Emily / procurement can see the trade-offs.

Edits we recommend:
- Keep baseline at 99.95% for hosted API, but add an alternate commitment for Dedicated (reserved capacity): 99.97% uptime and a 30-day rolling SLA review for unusually spiky traffic patterns.
- Latency: keep p50 < 80ms, tighten p95 to < 300ms for payment-critical routes if they’re pinned to Dedicated capacity (we can provide differentiated SLIs per route as an exhibit).
- Remedy/credit structure: revise the band percentages down slightly to reduce financial tail-risk while keeping customer protection: 99.95-99.90 => 4% credit; 99.90-99.50 => 12%; <99.50 => 30%; monthly cap at 50% of monthly fees for hosted customers, and 75% cap for Dedicated because of higher guarantees.
- Maintenance carveouts: propose a two-tier carveout process — standard notice (72 hours) and an "exception carveout" for emergency ops where we notify within 4 hours and provide post-incident remediation credit if the emergency extends beyond 4 hours.

Operational notes:
- We should explicitly exclude experimental kernel updates and high-risk quantization rollouts from uptime calculations for customers who opt into early access; those customers sign an "early access" addendum.
- Can we add a clause that automatic model fallbacks (compatible model variants) are considered mitigations and not SLA breaches unless they cause >30m of degraded performance? (Avery — that was in your note; I think we should keep it.)

Attachments for pricing/legal: uptime-metrics.csv (sample), draft_credit_table.xlsx (will upload to Drive).

Priyom, if you can confirm the monthly cap numbers from procurement side and add any phrasing we need for G/A accounting, we’ll push the updated exhibit to legal.

Thanks — Ben

From: Emily Thomas <emily.thomas@peregrinefin.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@peregrinefin.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Baseline SLA and maintenance carveouts - quick acceptance + carveout request

Avery / Ben — thanks for the clear breakdown and the adjustments. Procurement reviewed Ben's revised caps and the dedicated uplift options. A few quick items before legal moves to DocuSign: 

1) Uptime: For Dedicated (reserved capacity) we want to accept 99.97% as proposed. For Hosted, we can accept 99.95% if the monthly credit cap is 60% (higher than your 50%) — this is our negotiating position given the business impact of outages to settlement flows.

2) Latency: We’ll sign up to differential SLIs per route. For payment-critical routes on Dedicated, we expect p95 < 300ms. Please include a definition section clarifying that latency is measured at the API gateway egress and excludes customer-side network variance.

3) Maintenance carveouts: We accept the 72-hour standard notice. For emergency carveouts, we need a formal "post-incident remediation credit" clause: if an emergency maintenance event that you trigger (or is a product-side patch) affects availability > 4 hours, we expect an escalating credit (an additional 10% for each 4-hour block beyond the initial four, up to the monthly cap).

4) DocuSign and timeline: procurement asked for a DocuSign-ready exhibit and asked to receive it by next Wednesday (2027-05-19) to keep our onboarding timeline. Please include the appendix that documents the 02:00-06:00 UTC operational buffer and how batching pipelines are scoped.

If you can send the revised exhibit (and the DocuSign link) we’ll route to legal and procurement. Once we have that, we’ll likely have only minor redlines.

Best regards,
Emily Thomas
Head of Platform Risk, Peregrine Financial
emily.thomas@peregrinefin.com
